Police were told that the boy had picked it up on the road. The men were asked if anyone supported the boy's statement and the boy's uncle stepped forward. The uncle was taken to one side by one of the policemen. A burst of gunfire was heard, and the uncle fell. "The men were told to dress and face the water. With their backs to the police, they were told to walk into the water. They were shoulder to shoulder. One of those who was among the group of men in the water heard an order given in Serbia to shoot. As shooting began, he was one of the first to plunge into the water. He was up to his waist as men fell all around him. A policeman went over to one man who was crying for help, fired again and killed him." You see, we can go into it all again but we don't need to. This is an account of a grave crime in your general area of responsibility, and you can't help us with it at all, I take it.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you absolutely nothing about it because this is information which was not gathered on the spot. This is one-sided information collected in Albania. You are relying on the OSCE, but this is information gathered on the basis of hearsay. I was there on that day and the following day until the activities were concluded, and I have not heard of anything like this. I have not seen anything like this. You are referring to the OSCE, wishing to make this information appear legitimate, but I'm telling you that this is one-sided information gathered in Albania by persons who had fled from Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if Mr. Nort would turn over to page 278, the left-hand side of it. And this is additional to what came from the live witnesses in Court, because they'd all left the village. We read the paragraph to this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. effect: "Surviving villagers who'd either remained or failed to escape Bela Crkva were eventually expelled from the village on or around the 16th of April when the police entered at approximate 1500 hours and told everyone to leave in 30 minutes, under threat of being killed by the VJ. Later the same day, three large, heavily armed groups of soldiers with paint on their faces entered the village. The police forced two young brothers to undress. They fired their guns close to the boys, then released them after forcing them to hand over DM 1.060. As everyone was leaving the village, the police burned the houses after looting them, and cars were confiscated. Villagers were beaten, and police and VJ threw stones at them." What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that this is all pure fabrication. You are mixing up the police and the army. One moment it's the police doing something, the next moment it's the army. You mentioned the 16th of April; is that right? The 16th of April. I know where my units were and my troops on the 16th of April, and no one was even a few kilometres near Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll see what your war diary says in a minute or so. It's taking some time to review it. But the evidence we've had gives an account of the burial of these people, and then there's evidence that's before the Court, it's Exhibit 168, showing how a forensic team, a British forensic team, I see, on the 30th of June and between then and the 3rd of July of 1999 performed 59 -- 54 post-mortem examinations on 42 identified and 12 unidentified victims from Bela Crkva, and in 98 per cent of those cases death was by gunshot wounds. Now, that's a large number of people on your area of responsibility to be killed by gunshot wounds in an area where you say, as I understand it, no person would have died in that way. Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you are saying, that a large number of people were killed there from firearms, this means nothing to me. I know where my units were on each day and what they were doing. And if forensic experts established that someone had been killed by firearms, this still doesn't mean that they know who did the shooting, whether the army, the KLA, or whether it happened in some other ways. I am responsible only for the actions of my units. I have explained how my units acted in Bela Crkva, and I even illustrated this graphically. And there is also my report which I submitted to the corps command.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't recall everything, but I don't remember Mr. Nice having provided a forensic report of the English team in connection with Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Was that done, Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Unless my records are incorrect and, if so, I'll correct it at the break, he has been provided indeed with the exhibit number that I gave him. 98, I think I said it was. And it will, of course, be an exhibit in the case. I'll call for it and we'll see what it amounts to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's just have a little think about this book. We'll come back to the book in a second. If we go through the Bela Crkva pages in your file, which take us from 360 to 366, we find, of course, nothing contemporaneous of any kind, do we?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are all statements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nothing contemporaneous of any kind. A simple question. Nothing contemporaneous with the events of any kind?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything connected to these events is contained here. It's all explained. It's all explained in writing and also in diagrams.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You remember yesterday when asked about this book here, you said you brought it in case the Defence wanted it, and you were reluctant, weren't you, to hand it over?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm willing to hand it over but in the proper way. I haven't brought it here to give it to you. I brought it here in case I needed it. You could have received it through the Defence if the Defence requires it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are three possibilities for this book that I want you to consider, and I may ask the learned Judges to consider in due course, depending on your answers. One is that it's a contemporaneous and properly kept book; two is that it was contemporaneous but that it certainly wasn't properly kept when it excluded reference to matters of the kind into which we are inquiring; and the third is that it wasn't contemporaneous at all and was constructed since. Let's deal with one point straight away. Recognising as you did when I showed you the letters that this is a document that the OTP has been seeking for many years, can you give any explanation as to why it wasn't available? Was it in some sense lost or mislaid or overlooked? Any reason why it shouldn't have been provided years ago?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for my documents, I said that in 2001 or 2002. No document from my brigade is in dispute, and each one can be submitted. In my bag I have a request made by you for me to get the document out of the archives. I cannot go and say, "Give me my diary." One has to find the record of the documentation in the archives. You have to know the file number. You have to be able to locate the diary in the archives. You have to know what folder it's in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a long answer, but it was a simple question. Was -- and I'm going to rephrase it: Was there any practical impediment or obstruction that made it impossible for this book to be provided before we saw it yesterday?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is absolutely no obstacle, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I wonder if Mr. Nort would be good enough to come and take this book and hand it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The disposition of your troops on -- at the area of Bela Crkva on the 25th of March is something, of course, that should be recorded in this diary, isn't it? Can you just help us with the reference there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entry for the 25th is as follows: "The areas are in there -- the troops are in their places of deployment and they are acting pursuant to the alert. At 5.00, the commander went to the positions in the area of Retimlje to destroy the Siptar forces there. At 1100 hours, a signal was given, an air raid warning, rather, was given. At 1200 hours, our barracks were attacked by NATO. The civilian MUP facility was hit with three rockets. A rocket hit the Ceja facility. The consequences were such that none of our men were injured. During the combat operations three men were slightly wounded, one was seriously wounded. They were transported to the Nis military hospital. The morale of the men and officers is high, and the rear and logistics are acting according to plan." This is what was recorded on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that covers Bela Crkva or not?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This covers that entire day, and Bela Crkva was covered by my order, my map, and my analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does -- Mr. Delic, maybe you're having trouble with a proposition that I'm advancing, and if so, we must get over the problem. Do you understand the difference between a contemporaneous record and a document that's been written years later?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I absolutely understand that, but this is a document that was written at the material time, and it is the way it's been written. Now, whether it's of top quality is a completely different question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it contain any reference to the operation that you say was lawful in Bela Crkva on the 15th, 16th of April -- I beg your pardon, on the 25th of March? Does it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operations are mentioned where the brigade is involved. Bela Crkva is not mentioned because there were no operations in Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Retimlje is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Retimlje or, rather, the entire operation is called Retimlje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look at one other detail and then I'll ask for the book back, please. According to the analysis of "As Seen, As Told," it was on the 16th of April that armed groups of soldiers and the VJ arrived. Can you -- we haven't done this yet. Can you find us the 16th of April in your diary, your war diary? Find it.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, here it is, the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for completeness, does that -- read it to yourself or -- I don't want to take time reading it out loud. Does that contain any reference to VJ forces being -- your forces being in the area of Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm reading the entire entry for the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please be asked to read slower. The interpreters do not have the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, please read more slowly for the benefit of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My only -- I don't desire you to read it in full. We will have the resources to review it at some stage, I hope. I just simply want to know if it makes any reference to your forces going to Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no reference because my forces didn't go to Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'm going to necessarily pass over various parts of the detail. Landovica I'm going to pass over. But if we could now turn to binder 6 and go to 395, we come to Suva Reka. If I could have the -- if Mr. Nort could bring me back that document, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again if we look at 395, we have an untranslated document. 395 is the statement of -- statement to the commission made in March of 1999. And who is it by, please, Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said the document was 395?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not written when you said it was. It was written on the 15th of January, 2003.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose document is this?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a statement of Colonel Stojan Konjikovac, at that time commander of combat group 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the next statement, which is also still untranslated. 396, 397, similarly 2003 statement 398, similarly all untranslated, 399, all untranslated, until we get to 400, untranslated; 401, still untranslated; 402, still untranslated, and then we come to the next map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I simply draw to your attention that it is quite impossible to deal in any detail with a case advanced in documents of this kind if they are untranslated as late in the stage as this. I simply have not had the time or resources to have even draft translations done of these for our own benefit and therefore wholly in the dark with what they say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I can deal with Suva Reka comparatively briefly with you, Mr. Delic. Again, no contemporaneous record of any kind apart from what may exist in the war diary that we were looking at. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We do not have any other documentation. We have the orders, we have the maps, we have the small map, the statement made by me and the statement made by the commander who passed through Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course somebody else has all the other documents, the intelligence listening records, the reports up and down the chain of command, and any other daily diaries or records that were kept by the units answering to you. We -- somebody else has those. We don't have them.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's absolutely no other documentation. Everything that these combat groups had, those that were in the area, and since I was in the area, too, they reported to me personally. All of this is radio communication. And upon completion of operations, then an analysis was written and sent on to the corps command. You are alluding that something has been hidden. There is no need to hide anything. This was a perfectly legitimate operation that was carried out on orders from the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did this group of senior officers sitting round a table for the VJ commission, how did they really think that the OTP and the learned Judges would be assisted by what we can describe in a sense as secondhand material, that is material that's drafted after the event, rather than the raw material, war diaries, matters of that sort, when the OTP had been pressing the authorities for that raw material day in and day out? How did your group think that this was a better way of presenting the material?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You obviously don't understand how the military functions. An army has its own regulations, and one knows exactly what is done and what kind of documents are kept in the army. There are no other documents about this event that somebody now put aside. This was not done for your benefit. This was addressed to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you understand the word "contemporaneous"?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All documentation is here that is contemporaneous and has already been shown to this Court, everything that pertains to this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you understand the word "contemporaneous," Mr. Delic? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if you understand what you're saying. I fully understand what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is a record that comes from one of your sub-units to you written on the day in question saying, "We did this, we found that," is that something that is contemporaneous?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are combat groups, units of reinforced companies that do not keep such documents. Since I was in the field, they reported to me either personally or through radio communications. A single report was sent to the command after completing the operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think this may be either new or different, Mr. Delic, from what you told us at the beginning when we looked at the regulations for the various records that had to be kept. Are you now saying that there were no other written records of any kind extant at the time that these documents were prepared?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Really, Mr. Nice, you should think before you put questions, or you were absent during all these days. I'm going to tell you what tabs are from that relevant time and that pertain to this period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I think, if you wouldn't mind, we'll have an answer to my question. It was a very simple one. And would you like, please, to open your bundle at tab 395. No. Let's go to --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine. I just want to tell you that what you have been talking about is in tab -- what you have been talking about is in tab 356, 357, tab 358, and tab 359. These are documents from the relevant time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's see what we've got here. One is the Joint Command order, which we've spent a lot of time on, dated the 23rd of March, and that's what was planned to happen. 358 is -- that's 356. 357 is another command, your command of the same date, planning what is to happen. 358 is a map setting out what you say was planned to happen. 359 is a document of the 30th of March and is a record of some events. Now -- and indeed it deals with Velika Krusa but we'll possibly come back and look at that, and Retimlje. Apart from 359, which, incidentally, has strictly confidential number, I see, but no number on it. Can you help us with that? What's its serial number? It says "strictly confidential number" but then it doesn't actually give a number.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot explain that except if this number was written in pencil and was therefore lost in photocopying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from 359, to the extent that it covers the matters we're looking at, is there any other contemporaneous document that you can turn us to that deals with Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no other document that deals with Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that there were no bits of paper left that said such things as report from you -- one of the units to you as the commander setting out what happened? No such bits of paper were left? Is that what you're now saying?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I'm saying. I'm saying that units kept those documents that they were ordered to keep. In one of the previous binders there was an order stating that an order had to exist, a map, and also an analysis of the operation carried out. That is the only thing that we were told to do for each and every operation. That is the order of the superior command. It is in one of the tabs that have already been shown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to -- and we've had your answers on records you kept right at the beginning of cross-examination. Let's go to 395. It's not your statement but it doesn't matter, and it's not translated but it doesn't matter because there are two points on this statement that are self-apparent even to the non-reader of Serbian. First -- have you got 395 there? First, this statement and all these statements, as far as I can understand it --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- makes no reference by footnote - and you've done your doctoral thesis so you know about footnotes - by footnote or otherwise to the sources on which it relies, does it? It doesn't say I've looked at this record, I've looked at that record for this detail, see report so-and-so. No reference to records at all.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why is it necessary at all for a person who was on the spot to have this kind of information? He himself was a source of information and describes his activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you see, although we haven't yet got the advantage of a translation, and although of course we don't read Serbian let alone in Cyrillic, we only have to look at the first paragraph to see that there's references to 1200 hours, in the next paragraph to 1800 hours, I think, the next paragraph to 1300 hours, just as one of the details this document provides in 2003, looking back four years. Where did the person get that sort of detail from if, as you are now saying, there were no written records?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, is it necessary for a person who directly commanded that unit to have something jog his memory regarding these details? I recall all details from the war period. Perhaps sometimes I forget a name or may forget a name, but I remember all the details. Mr. Nice, you did not survive bombing by NATO whereas I did, together with my commanders and officers. Only a few of these details are mentioned, a few different points in time, and to me this looks like a perfectly normal thing, the usual kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's now look at the evidence about Suva Reka because we don't have the advantage of translation of your account in detail, or your officers' account in detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are there any better examples than this, Mr. Nice, that might illustrate the point? In other words, statements that have been translated?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'll try and find something over the break. It's a point that only occurred to me in light of the witness's answer about there being no records, but I will try to find some more, and we will look up for the dates upon which we have got evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what do you say happened at Suva Reka, in a sentence, on the 24th of March and thereabouts, 25th of March?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 24th of March I was not in Suva Reka. On the 25th of March, my unit only passed through Suva Reka. My unit was not involved in any operations or any activities in Suva Reka except for the fact that they passed through Suva Reka and went in the direction of the village of Rastane. In a tab that was provided here, that can be seen even on a diagram.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, yes. And when did you return to Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tab 427 shows my unit, and it shows where my unit was at a certain point in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you see, tab 427 was prepared sometime in 2002, 2003, when there were no other records, apparently, around. So somebody's working from memory or -- I don't know what they're working from. You tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Nort would like to put this on the overhead projector so that we can display how detailed is the map that was prepared by the VJ commission in 2002 and 2003 when there were no written records around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying this document was prepared, what, just from memory?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was not only prepared from memory. It was based on the four relevant documents that I just mentioned. What you are saying, that this is a good map, well, of course we use good maps. 1:50000, where you can see something. We don't use the kind of maps that you display and that may mislead witnesses. This is a military map, and the scale is 1:50000. This is an excerpt that shows Suva Reka. There is nothing I see here that confirms what you've been saying. The unit left at such-and-such a time from the garrison, they arrived at such-and-such a time before Suva Reka, and at the time that was mentioned in the order they arrived at their basic position. They only obeyed the orders that were given at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened in the next few days at Suva Reka; anything or nothing?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as my unit is concerned, nothing happened in Suva Reka because my unit only passed through Suva Reka and continued its combat operations as envisaged in the order I gave and the order that came from the corps. This unit that passed through Suva Reka on the 27th moved towards the village of Dobrodeljane and the following day towards the village of Pagarusa. This unit did not return this way through Suva Reka, rather via Pagarusa, the village of Milanovac, it got out to the Malisevo-Orahovac road and took that road back to the Prizren garrison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The evidence includes evidence from Shyhrete Berisha - you made some reference to that witness - Halit Berisha and Hysni Berisha and Agron Berisha, who described the terrible massacre that occurred there. Now, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. what do you say about that massacre?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Last time I said what I knew about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... recorded, please.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That has nothing to do with my unit or with the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first learn about this apparent private feud that led to this extraordinary tragedy? When did you first learn about it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I learnt about that after the war. I knew some things earlier on, too, but I did not link them up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us about what you learnt earlier on and where you learnt it; who told you, where you read it, all that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From earlier on I knew that the person I mentioned then had a motel of his own. That is not something that can be contested. That is something that everyone living in that territory knows. Also, I knew that two or three assassination attempts were made against that person's life. One was either the end of 1998 or the beginning of 1999. I learnt about that as a matter of course during my informal meetings with the chief of MUP when this person was wounded and when the vendor at the kiosk where he was buying cigarettes was killed. At the time the OSCE came, when passing there, I saw that the OSCE team was put up at that locality. But at that time I did not link up the two. This was one of the possibilities, for the mission to be staying there. Later on, when going to Pristina -- rather, to Dulje, I saw that the mission had moved elsewhere. Again, I did not make any connection because I thought that there were more members of the mission who came and that they needed accommodation elsewhere too. That's what I thought at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Time for the break. We will adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, a couple of outstanding queries. The accused's concern about evidence of post-mortem on the bodies at the last site is contained in, as I said, Exhibit 168, which is the expert report of Baccard which itself is synthesised or summarised by a number of other medicolegal analyses resulting from forensic missions in Kosovo in 1999. In response to His Honour Judge Bonomy's question about one of the 2002, 2003 statements that have been translated that might contain some details, Your Honours might generally like to look at about 369 and thereabouts. 369 itself is quite a good example. It's Vlatko Vukovic, the battalion commander we've been hearing about, and on that particular one, if you look at it you will see several references to times and various other details, some of which might be obtained from a map, some of which might not. There are others of that kind there, although it's true to say that the vast majority of these statements have not yet -- have not yet been produced in translated form. Your Honours, the next administrative matter is although we were able to do some work on the document produced by the witness as a war diary in court, it would help us to have a copy of it. May it be returned to the Registry at the end of this session, and may we be provided with a copy of it for working on later today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Returning to Suva Reka, Mr. Delic, there was a Defence witness, Hutsch, who gave evidence of artillery support being present in the area and of houses being on fire. Can you explain that? 28th of March, 1999, is the relevant date.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said a Defence witness, did you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to be more specific when you say artillery support and houses were burning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... get the transcript out and I'll do that maybe. Just tell us this: Was there any artillery support being deployed on the 28th of March in the area of Suva Reka? If so, how near?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say the Suva Reka area, Suva Reka is a municipality, a broader area, and the artillery was deployed but it was deployed towards the defence lines which are located between the village of Dobrodeljane and Pagarusa, along my axis, but it was deployed along the axes of other units too, so I'd have to take a look at the map to be able to answer that, and it wasn't my brigade then. As far as my brigade is concerned, it was deployed probably the Rad [phoen] feature and towards the village of Pagarusa, the mountain there, which is the opposite side of Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it may be helpful if at this stage in any event we look at the quality of your war diary generally so the Court can know what we're dealing with. Perhaps if Mr. Nort would lay it on the overhead projector for two days before the 16th of March. And we'll then look at that and the next two days, bearing in mind you just spoke about your troops being deployed in Pagarusa. Let's just see the totality of your war diary. 26th of March, Prizren, between midnight and midnight. Would you be good enough, please, to read out the entries for us and they'll be interpreted for us.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "A blockade is under way of the STS in the village of Retimlje area in cooperation with the MUP units, electronic interference on the part of NATO is being undertaken, a blockade is under way of the STS in the area of Dobrodeljane and Pagarusa village."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there is a blockade, is there, at Pagarusa? Next page, please, Mr. Nort. Pagarusa is where exactly? Just remind myself.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pagarusa is to the north of Dobrodeljane, towards Malisevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you'd like to read the 27th.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Activities are continuing to break up the STS in the area of Retimlje and the Dobrodeljane-Pagarusa axis. NATO aviation is reconnoitering and is functional against the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the next entry. 28th. If you push it up the page a bit.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to read the whole diary, Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, I repeat: I don't object to your making observations like that. They don't distress me or upset me, if that's what you're seeking to do, but it does take time. Would you please read the entry for the 28th of March.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Activities are continuing to break up the STS in the region of Dobrodeljane Pagarusa. NATO aviation is constantly reconnoitering and electronically interfering and and targeting barracks targets."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this -- so first of all, the thing we can see is there is absolutely no reference there at all to action in the Suva Reka area.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dobrodeljane and Pagarusa are on the territory of Suva Reka, and that's what's mentioned. Suva Reka is not mentioned because that is not where my forces were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So you say that's the general area but it's not dealt with specifically. The second point we can see is that at this stage, and it may change later on and I'm not going to ask you to read any more for the time being, if we just go back to the top of the page, we can see the 28th is very similar in form to, and it's a very short form, to the 27th. Was this really the only headquarters record that was being kept?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The only records. And you forget, Mr. Nice, that my barracks was destroyed during those days, and my command had to move from one feature to another and saw where best to put up and establish new communication lines in view of the fact that both my telecommunications centre was hit too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So my whole barracks were --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No documents -- [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- were destroyed. The documents that existed, or part of the documents, were certainly destroyed in the barracks, but they were documents that are not relevant to this period and don't address this matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They weren't destroyed in the bombing, were they, because you've been able to produce all your pre-existing maps that lined the wall, showing what the plan was. So you can't be suggesting that there were documents destroyed.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But we can say that the people were not able to keep diaries or records in the detailed way that should have been done. So these are just short remarks that they managed to jot down during those days because there was constant bombing from the 24th onwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning of your questioning by me I took you to the relevant provisions of the book which you said was a textbook, and you gave an account that, unless we misunderstood it, explained that, yes, records were kept from your sub-units to you and from you up. Didn't up say that on that earlier occasion?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, quite correct, and I stand by that now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... what you're trying to say, unless I misunderstood it, that records weren't being kept. Can you explain the difference?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you say, Mr. Nice. You hear something that I did not utter, it seems, and records were always kept. But at the time when my barracks were bombed and when my command was destroyed and when my communications centre was destroyed, you can see that it is somewhat different and that the entries are shorter, and that later on, as time passed, when the command was established at another location, then the records were kept the way they should be kept.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's just take one example because His Honour asked me about it, and I've forgotten the number I gave the Court, but -- 369. Thank you. Can you just look at 369, please. You see -- have you got 369 open in front of you? I don't think so. It doesn't look like that to me, I don't think. 369.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ah. Well, there's a -- I think there may be a problem here. The 369 I've got in translation is from Vlatko Vukovic but the 369 you're looking at is from whom? Oh, yes, it's Vlatko Vukovic with the name reversed. Right. Now, if you look at this document here that Vukovic prepared in January 2003, he deals with some details, and if you look down, say, to the third paragraph, we see references to 0630 hours, 0730 hours, I went to the village at 1000 hours, 1400 hours I came across a group of civilians, 200 civilians in the group. Then over the page -- no, we needn't worry with over the page. That's his expressions about "As Seen, As Told." Where did Mr. Vukovic get the times to put them down in this statement?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic was there. He's a first-rate officer. He's not half-witted for anybody to have to remind him about what he did at what time, and I think he'll come into this Tribunal anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you think that he and all the other commanders and you did everything in these statements from memory, do you?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did have the relevant documents, such as orders by the brigade commander, a map, and an analysis. So that then was sufficient material for them to remind themselves of the activities at that time, and everybody wrote down their own statement to the best of their recollections, and there wasn't much time. I remember the entire war very vividly and each operation that I took part in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by the document analysis?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An analysis of the operation. The third document that there should be, an analysis sent up to the superior officer after every operation or event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The relevant document of analysis, for example, for Suva Reka is where in the bundles? Can you tell me?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, an analysis of the overall operation is where I told you it was. An analysis for Suva Reka doesn't exist because, as far as my unit is concerned, nothing happened in Suva Reka, so you must understand this once and for all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... overall event in Suva Reka? So we can just see at the time what detail it contains.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This will make it the tenth time. This is the tenth time, Mr. Nice, that I'm showing you the same thing. From tab 356 --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been advised to take the attitude you take with me as a questioner or is it your own choice?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My attitude is proper. I am not provoking you as you are trying to provoke me, but it's not having any effect on me. We end with tab 3 -- from tab 356 to tab 359 inclusive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I should say, in all fairness, I see nothing improper in the witness's demeanour in the way he has answered you. You're cross-examining vigorously and he's also answering in similar manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If that's the view the Court takes, I will press on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, going back briefly just to number 369, that document records that there was some action, that Colonel Vukovic was involved in combat on the 25th of March with terrorists. Now, following -- following that action on the 25th of March, would he make a written report to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Because I was with him on the 25th of March. I was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, in a situation where you were not there and something of this nature occurred under the supervision of the colonel rather than you, would he be expected to report if there had been action between him and terrorists?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. Mr. Bonomy, let's make one thing clear: If we look at tab -- the tab I just mentioned a moment ago, in my order there, it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: 356, I think that is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 357. Yes, 357 it is. And if you look at point 9: "Regular reports should be sent daily by 1900 hours with the situation as at 1700 hours. Interim reports when the need arises, as necessary."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, where are these reports now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are oral reports. You must remember that. So they're oral reports by each commander to a combat group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It may be -- it may be in the translation again, but the verb "submit" would tend to suggest something in writing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Reports, when I am present with the commanders in the field, are sent orally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand, yes. But there must -- oh, you mean if you're in the field at all, even if you're several kilometres away, the reports would still be sent to you orally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. While we're altogether in a uniform system of communication and we're functioning in a united uniform system, the commanders report to me throughout the day and report about everything that is happening on their territory. And if you look at these tabs, then the action was always interrupted at 1800 hours, and so up to 1900 hours they were supposed to send their report -- to report as to what the situation in their units was. I knew about everything else because I was with them there and was able to follow and monitor their action. On the map that I showed you, I was at one particular point, location, it was a hill, and I was able to follow the units down below me, to see them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you not have somebody with you who actually recorded these communications as they came in to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That wasn't customary or usual, and that in actual fact never happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, to go back to 359, which you say is the analysis, and we've looked at it a couple of times before, if you were working on that document to prepare, for example, document 369, Vukovic's report which details what he did at the line of blockade and the times he did it, "right flank platoon and the police unit coming under fire from the Celine sector," and all that sort of thing and the timings of that, can we find all that in here? I'm not denying that it may be in there but it's your document and I want you to help us find it.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're interested in the analysis, are you? The analysis deals with how the action evolved from the 25th and ending with the 28th and 29th inclusive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred us to the analysis when I was pursuing the topic of the detail of tab 369, if you remember, one of the documents in translation that the Court had asked me to find as an example of one having detail in it. So 369 has the detail. You referred us to the analysis. Can we find in the analysis, tab 359, the detail contained in the statement 369?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An analysis is sent to the Pristina Corps, and it is not sent for that commander. What it says here is for the entire unit, and the analysis has been combined for the overall action, for all men and all combat groups. And in the analysis there is certain details that are not contained in any report. But an analysis is a general document. It is a general analysis not following just one commander but following the general operation and action day by day and what happened on what particular day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me just explain why I'm asking you these questions. I'm asking you because I suggested to you at page 77, line 7, asking you if you were saying that the commanders produced these statements from memory. You said, "They have the relevant documents such as the orders by the brigade commander, the map, and an analysis." I asked you what you meant by the analysis and you said -- because I wasn't aware that you were referring to this document, but you said, just to remind you, that you said that this will be the tenth time that you'd taken us to it, and then we came back to it. That's why I'm asking you the questions. Very simple. Now, does this analysis document contain material upon which Mr. Vukovic could have relied to write his statement?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly contains elements which relate not only to Vukovic but to all the commanders. If you take a look, you will see that the analysis is a detail, but it doesn't deal with any commander separately but deals with the entire operation, all the combat action, and contains a great number of details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It's quite a long document. Incidentally, you had time to write this analysis at the time, although it has no confidential number on it but you didn't have time to write substantial entries in the war diaries. Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This analysis is written by the operations officer, the operative, and he -- this time this was written by Colonel Konjikovac who was head of the operational organ. The war diary was kept by the duty officer, and he was located in the unit, and he had other things to attend to, so the analysis was compiled after the combat operations had been concluded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll just take one paragraph from 369. On the 25th of March -- if you'd look at 369. 369. Keep your finger in 359. On the 25th of March, third paragraph -- fourth paragraph: "On the 25th of March... after the completion of a march, BG-2 took the line of blockade: Brod elevation trig point 432 tt - 440 by 0630 hours. The first contact with STS was at about 0730 when the right flank platoon and police unit came under fire from the village of Celine sector. Fire was returned. The fighting lasted for under an hour when the STS were routed and probably retreated to the village of Randubrava. The village was searched by the police unit. I went through the village at about 1000 hours and did not find the civilian population there." Can we find that if we come back to 359? Can we find any of those details? Probably here but I just can't -- or maybe they're not there.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't find details like this in a general document sent to the corps command. The document would have to be huge if it were to include what every squad or company leader saw on his axis. This is a general analysis, describing how the combat operation was conducted as a whole, what forces were engaged, what the enemy forces were, and how the combat took place. This is a lower-level commander describing his axis on only one day only for his unit. And what he is referring to accounts for 10 or 15 per cent of the overall forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we have the war diary back, please, or the document described as the war diary on the overhead projector. You asked for the transcript of the witness, the Defence witness Hutsch who, asked questions about where he was between the 25th and the 28th of March, said this, and I'll read it slowly: "I saw the aftereffects of Suva Reka around the 28th. At that time, it was clear that there had been attacks from the north, from the heights around the Dulje pass, down into Suva Reka. It was also clear, and I'd actually been able to hear that, that the artillery positions at Dulje pass had provided artillery support for an attack on Suva Reka. It was also clear that at that time houses were on fire, particularly on the margins of the village. There were also isolated houses on fire. I saw them with my own eyes." Well, now --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What witness are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a man called Hutsch, and he was called by the accused and who was serving the purpose of a journalist, a form of journalist. Now, what can you tell us that would explain that evidence?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything I can say runs completely contrary to this. The artillery was never pointed towards Suva Reka. Suva Reka was never targeted from any kind of artillery because our forces were in Suva Reka throughout this time, police forces and the local government authorities. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. As for my unit, I said that operations were carried out from the village of Rastane towards the village of Studencani, the village of Dobrodeljane, and the village of Pagarusa. Artillery fire was directed in a direction opposite from Suva Reka. As for this unit, it was facing Malisevo and moving parallel to my unit but in the opposite direction from Suva Reka. In 1998 and 1999, Suva Reka was never the object of any kind of shelling. And there were police forces there throughout this time. It was never under threat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or is the reality that you and the police were engaged in an unrecorded exercise in ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Were we perhaps fighting with the police? Were we fighting among ourselves? I do not challenge that this witness heard artillery fire. What I do challenge absolutely is that a single shell or grenade ever landed in Suva Reka, especially one fired by my unit. Why would someone fire on a town in which there were state authorities and the police, in which there were never any problems, which had never been taken by the terrorists? I simply fail to understand this. There's no logic in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question on Suva Reka is this: You know, don't you, about bodies being found in Batajnica and Petrovo Selo and elsewhere in Serbia coming from Kosovo. Can you explain how it should be that bodies from Suva Reka, within your area of responsibility, were subsequently found in Batajnica?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army has nothing to do with Batajnica. I read in the newspapers about what you have just mentioned, and I also heard that it was mentioned before this Tribunal, but I have no knowledge of it, and I simply don't know how bodies from Suva Reka could have ended up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Remind us, please, what is the premises at Batajnica upon which these bodies were found?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You should tell me that. I know they were found in Batajnica somewhere close to the Danube, in a location there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have no idea what sort of property they were found on, what sort of premises? Really?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for Batajnica, I do know the village or town of Batajnica, but I'm not familiar with the banks of the Danube there. I know that we have certain facilities in Batajnica, an airport and electronic surveillance equipment. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's go back. For you and/or the police to dig up bodies and move them from Kosovo to Batajnica would be quite a large exercise, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for me, I would give up right away. I am not an undertaker, and I would never ever engage in such morbid activities, nor would my unit. As for this, I reject any possibility that my units were involved in such activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The activity -- let's assume -- it's a matter for the Judges in due course. Let's assume that the activity happened. Somebody did it. My question to you was carefully phrased. It would be quite a large exercise, whoever did it, to dig bodies up, put them in trucks, drive them up to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly it would be a major undertaking, and anyone doing such a thing would have a purpose, a goal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were only two bodies on the ground exercising authority, because you've told us there were no paramilitaries. They were the army and the police.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever I mention paramilitaries, I am absolutely certain of this with respect to my own area of responsibility, although the orders were the same for the entire territory of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is yes, there were just the two bodies exercising authority. If it was the police who engaged in this exercise of digging up bodies and taking them to a military or near to a military establishment at Batajnica, they would run the risk of being surprised by the army, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you are saying now are insinuations. You mention military facilities. You mention the police. Let's understand each other: The police and the army are not authorities. They are state organs, but they are not exercising authority. That's not how I understand them. They are simply organs with certain competencies. The police has to secure public law and order and the army has to secure the state borders and the state. They are not exercising authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Who else apart from the police and the army on your part of Kosovo could ever have organised logistically the digging up of bodies and the carting of them away to Serbia? Who else apart from the army or the police?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly wasn't done by the army, and I'm sure it wasn't done by the police either. If it was done --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please - you were there, you keep telling us we weren't - can you identify any other body, organisation, group that could have dug up bodies buried in typically public places and take them to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This question implies that a previous question has been clarified. It could be put to the witness if Mr. Nice has evidence that this happened while the witness was there. He is claiming that the witness was there when it took place. What if it all happened afterwards? It came out in the newspapers in the spring of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us hear whether the witness can answer the question. Are you in a position to answer the question, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the transferral of the bodies, I cannot answer any questions about this because the army did not engage in such activities, and I believe neither did the police. The fact that it was only mentioned in 2001 might provide an answer to some of the questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My final question on this point which I'd like you to answer, the same basis as the others, is if it's the case that the police moved the bodies, they would have to have the knowledge and complicity of the army to avoid being surprised and stopped in what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, this is quite like your other insinuations that the army and the police were together doing something that was illegal. I absolutely reject such a possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as to the accused's interjection, the Kumanovo agreement was in June 1999, and so from that moment on neither the VJ nor the MUP had access to the territory, did they?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were there until that agreement.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- apart from bodies going from Suva Reka to Serbia, bodies from Meja went there as well, also in your area of responsibility as I must suggest. I think this is material that has come to light since the close of the Kosovo case, but nevertheless I think it's a matter of public record. Bodies from Meja went to Serbia. And, Mr. Delic, I'm going to suggest to you in clear terms in light of all that you say about the authority of the police, the absence of paramilitaries, that the movement of those bodies must have been done with your knowledge and consent.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are absolutely not right. You are not right. What you are saying has nothing to do with my work or my actions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course you were jointly engaged with the police, weren't you, on many occasions?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police is a state organ with its own competencies, and the nature of the activities in 1998 and 1999 was such that at certain points in time we had to cooperate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look, please, on the overhead projector at the first of two entries that use the word "asanacija," and I'd like you to read the entries and then to explain them to us, please. The first one, as we can see, it's not very clear but it's the best we can do, is the 4th of May. Would you like to read that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The brigade commander warned the subordinate units in the area of responsibility about the irreproachable organisation of work, discipline and complete combat control of the territory --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The 2nd Motorised Battalion --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: General, the interpreters are asking you to speak more slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "... engaged in engineering work in the area of defence and the sanitisation of the terrain. The morale of the unit is very high. The armoured battalion..." and so on and so forth. What is your question, Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we look at -- pause for a minute. Now can we go to the second entry that Mr. Nort has. If you could just turn it over. There's another one where the word "asanacija" is used. Can you find the date for this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Go back a page, please, Mr. Nort, and we'll just see what date is there, and then we'll come back to that paragraph. What is the date on that page? I can't see it at the moment. Ah, there it is. This appears to be the 18th of May. Over the page, please, Mr. Nort. Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this entry here, I think it's in the -- maybe the next paragraph. Could you read a little more slowly for the interpreters, please.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you want me to read?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think -- I can't see on this the "asanacija" word. I think it may be in the second paragraph. If you can see it, that's the paragraph I want you to read.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The 2nd Battalion reported that work was focused on engineering and obstacle construction in the area and the destruction of unexploded projectiles. Sanitisation of the territory was carried out. The morale in the unit is securing or is making possible the carrying out of the task."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, these are sanitisation, or asanacija. What did that mean?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Asanacija" implies clearing up a territory, clearing it of corpses, of people or animals, carcasses, unexploded projectiles, toxic materials, and everything else that might pose a threat to the population of that territory or members of the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that work you did alone or with the police?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Primarily the military carried out asanacija in terms of what it was trained to do: Removing carcasses of dead animals, because there were huge numbers of dead animals all over the territory; killing and removing stray dogs; and something that only the army was able to do, destroying unexploded cluster bombs and other dangerous materials. If you continue reading, you shall see --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm afraid we can't mark the book yet because we haven't got our own copy for marking. Now, if you look at these next pages, and I think Mr. Nort is having to be careful that the book doesn't come to pieces. Now, this one I think you'll find a reference here to a joint activity with the police. Can you find it and then read it out to us, please. It starts at the top, I think.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please turn back to the previous page?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Nort, could you turn it back to the previous page, please. 16th of May it looks like, unless it changes the date --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just -- could you scroll up a little bit, please. Very well. This is about Hoca Zagradska. He also reported that "part of the unit --" and now you can turn the page and scroll down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. What does that passage say about a joint activity?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "-- started clearing up the terrain in cooperation with the MUP. The morale of the fighters is good." And we have a tab referring to this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pause there. So that's clearing up the terrain in cooperation with the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Next page, please, Mr. Nort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this one has got another reference, I think, to joint operations with the MUP. Can we find it? It may be further down. It's where the yellow sticker is, probably.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does this say?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's nothing in dispute here. All the units are in the areas that have been taken. Parts of the units of the brigade, in cooperation with the MUP, are clearing up the STS -- from the STS, and then there's a sticker there so I can't read it. Remove the sticker.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Nort, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "In the broader area --" can you turn the page, please. Could you scroll down, please. "In the broader area of Tusus."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And then the last entry, please, Mr. Nort, of the three I asked you to point out. Again, take the sticker off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this one refers to a joint MUP operation. Can you read it out, please.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you move it a bit? This is what it says -- could you please turn the previous page. Could you turn to the previous page, please. And the end. A bit more. "The 3rd Battalion reported that a part of the unit acting on the commander's orders was engaged in clearing up the terrain in cooperation with the MUP forces of the Siptar forces." We have been through the tab, and we have seen the order and the analysis and the map pertaining to this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we've got examples here of joint activity with the MUP in clearing the terrain, and that would include clearing the terrain of the dead bodies, wouldn't it, where there were any?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a pure fabrication of yours. It absolutely does not mean what you say. It's clearing the terrain of Siptar terrorist forces. It means joint action in combat. And we have seen the map, we have seen my order, we have shown the analysis. And I said that five of my men were killed or, rather, five men - three were soldiers and two were members of the MUP - on the 17th of May, and you are now equating fighting with removal of corpses. This is absolutely incorrect, and I have to tell you so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, then, what we should look for in your war diary if we seek an account of the army disposing of dead bodies killed in combat? What sort of entry should we be looking for?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are no entries about this because the army did not remove corpses of people. The army was unable to identify those who had been killed. This was done by the MUP. The army only removed carcasses of animals and also bombs and rockets and cluster projectiles, which were dangerous both for the population and the army. The identification of bodies was done by the MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you think of any way in which those bodies left Kosovo and went to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot think of any way, no. Except that somebody organised this with a special purpose in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will, with your leave, decide overnight whether I can leave my exploration of the crime sites with the two examples or three examples I've covered. I obviously can't cover them all but I do have a few questions to ask of a general nature in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Taking you back, please, to Croatia and your service there. You told us how your time in Croatia and your time in Bosnia, I think, counted for purposes of pension. As a matter of fact, did your time count at double rate, in the way that active service time counted?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that although as you would say you went as a volunteer on both occasions, in fact you were getting wartime benefits from your home military service, yes?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were not wartime benefits. I had a certificate stating that I had spent a certain period of time on a territory affected by a war. While I was in Croatia, there was still the JNA, and Croatia was then part of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, and I was there as a soldier of the JNA. On leaving that territory, I received a certificate which I forwarded to my personnel officer, and he calculated my time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What does double the rate mean? Does it mean that if you served six months there you would be -- you would have one year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Yes. If I was there for six months, it would be credited in terms of my pension as one year of service rather than six years [as interpreted]. In terms of service, it would be eight months. So time spent in a war situation is doubled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've accused one of your chiefs of general staff Perisic of being, I think, a traitor, but do you have any negative views about Veljko Kadijevic, an earlier top soldier in your army?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know Veljko Kadijevic personally. After all, he was in the army much earlier, and there is a great difference between our two ranks. So I never really had the opportunity of meeting him close up let alone hearing his views. However, General Perisic I saw several times because I was brigade commander, and I carried out --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were active -- Mr. Nort, please. You were active in Croatia. You told us of the apparently limited role you fulfilled. Kadijevic described the manoeuvre at Croatia in the following terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page, please, Mr. Nort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He said -- it deals with the stages, and he says: "The idea behind this manoeuvre embraced the following basic elements: "A total air and sea blockade of Croatia; "The directions of offences of the main forces of the JNA directly connected to the liberation of Serb regions in Croatia and JNA garrisons deep into Croatian territory. To this end, cut Croatia along the following lines: Gradiska-Virovitica; Bihac-Karlovac-Zagreb; Knin-Zadar; Mostar-Split. The strongest group of armoured motorised forces would liberate Eastern Slavonia and then move quickly westward, linking up with forces in Western Slavonia and proceeding on to Zagreb and Varacdin, that is towards the Slovene frontier." And then this: "At the same time, strong forces from the Herceg-Novi-Trebinje region would be used to block Dubrovnik from land and break out into the Neretva Valley, thus linking up operations with forces working along the Mostar-Split line." Now, that's what the Chief of the General Staff, in a published book, described as the purpose of the operations, including the purpose at Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This is an exhibit in the case, Your Honours. It's 4 -- 449A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that's his description and you've had the text to follow in Serbian. You were present not at Trebinje itself but at the -- no, no, no, not at Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were present in Cavtat, of course, and in the area of Dubrovnik. Is what you saw consistent with the plan described by your general?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What the general describes are attempts to safeguard the integrity of Yugoslavia. Of course, all members of the military and most of the citizens of this state were in favour of preserving the integrity of the state. Probably what the general wrote here are attempts related to that.
